What's so amazing about lions?

Called the "king of beasts," the lion is almost the only member of the cat family that lives in a group called a pride. The cooperation of the family is its biggest trait.

We've gathered all kinds of stories about lions here, including lion traits, the lion's mane, and the lion pride.

content.alt: Lion - Nature and science facts about lions
content.text:
Nature and science facts about lions

A male lion's full mane is a mark that shows his strength and health. Hunting is done mainly by the nimble females working together, and a strong sociability in which the whole pride raises the cubs together is a defining trait. The mighty roar carries for several kilometers, announcing the territory and calling the family. Surprisingly, the lion is a laid-back animal that spends much of the day resting in the shade of a tree.

Point out things like the mane (males), the pride, cooperative hunting (females), and the roar (communication). It's great to talk together about, "Why do lions live in a group?"

Parent guide — how to grow curiosity

Compare "the lion family hunts and raises cubs together" with your own family's cooperation. Finding the difference between the tiger (solitary) and the lion (pride) teaches the diversity of animals.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. Why do lions live in a group?
A. To hunt together and raise the cubs together. They're almost the only member of the cat family that lives in a group.

Q. Who does the hunting?
A. Mainly the nimble females, working together. The male's mane is a mark of strength and health.

Q. How can we observe them at home?
A. Comparing with your own family's cooperation, and finding the difference between the tiger (solitary) and the lion (pride), both work well.
